chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyād narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Dāwūd al-Ṭāʾī, from a man among our companions, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the muḥārib, and I said to him: Our companions say that the Imam has discretion regarding him: if he wishes, he amputates; if he wishes, he crucifies; and if he wishes, he kills.

So he said: “These are prescribed matters in the Book of Allah. If he kills and takes property, he is to be killed and crucified. If he kills and does not take property, he is to be killed. If he takes property and does not kill, his hand is amputated. And if he fled and was not overpowered, then was later seized, his hand is amputated—unless he repents; if he repents, then he is not amputated.”

key_terms.الْإِمَامَ: the legitimate authority who implements the prescribed ruling
key_terms.الْمُحَارِبِ: one who wages violent hostility and public armed aggression
key_terms.قُطِعَ: had the prescribed amputation carried out
key_terms.كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: the Quran as the source of the ruling
key_terms.يَتُوبَ: to repent and return from the offense

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a muḥārib in Shia hadith according to the Book of Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out the legal rulings concerning the muḥārib, explaining that the punishments are fixed according to the categories mentioned in the Book of Allah. The ruling distinguishes between killing, taking property, and fleeing, and it also notes the legal effect of repentance in one case.
